symbols.name: growth factor
symbols.meaning: The factor by which one recursion level multiplies the call parameter.
symbols.quote: Here $m$ is the growth factor of the parameter.

symbols.name: number of pieces
symbols.meaning: The number of pieces into which a call divides its volume, counting the pieces.
symbols.quote: Here $W$ is the number of pieces a call divides its volume into.

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The number of stored bits a call works on, counting the bits.
symbols.quote: A call works on a stored volume $V$, the number of stored bits it holds.

symbols.name: call parameter
symbols.meaning: The parameter of a call, which counts its field digits or selected axes.
symbols.quote: A call has a parameter $e$ that counts field digits or selected axes.

symbols.name: smaller-call count
symbols.meaning: The number of smaller calls that one call makes.
symbols.quote: Here $s$ is the number of smaller calls that one call makes, each on a stream of $V/W$ bits.

symbols.name: cost per unit volume
symbols.meaning: The time per unit volume of a call at parameter m^k.
symbols.quote: Let $F_k$ be the time per unit volume of a call at parameter $m^k$, which has $k$ levels of recursion beneath it.

symbols.name: recursion levels
symbols.meaning: The number of levels of recursion beneath a call, counting them.
symbols.quote: Let $F_k$ be the time per unit volume of a call at parameter $m^k$, which has $k$ levels of recursion beneath it.

symbols.name: call ratio
symbols.meaning: The ratio s/W of child calls to pieces.
symbols.quote: Set $\rho=s/W$, the ratio of child calls to pieces.

symbols.name: logarithm base m
symbols.meaning: The function sending x to the exponent t with m^t = x.
symbols.quote: Let $\log_m x$ denote the number $t$ with $m^t=x$.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent below one with a < m^tau, which sets the cost per unit volume.
symbols.quote: Here $\tau$ is the saving exponent, with $\rho<m^{\tau}$.

symbols.name: bit length of n
symbols.meaning: The number of bits of n, the ceiling of log2 n, counting them.
symbols.quote: Let $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ be the bit length of $n$.

symbols.name: working precision
symbols.meaning: The working precision in bits, equal to 6b.
symbols.quote: Here $p=6b$ is the working precision in bits, so $p=\Theta(\lg n)$.

symbols.name: axis bound
symbols.meaning: An upper bound on the number of selected axes of the numerical layer, counting axes.
symbols.quote: The numerical layer has a bound $d$ on its number of selected axes, with $d=\Theta(p^{\epsilon})$.

symbols.name: size exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent in d = Theta(p^epsilon), with 0 < epsilon < 1.
symbols.quote: Here $\epsilon$ is a fixed exponent with $0<\epsilon<1$.

symbols.name: padded box cell count
symbols.meaning: The number of cells of the padded box, the array the transforms act on.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ be the number of cells of the padded box, the array the transforms act on.

symbols.name: polynomial variable
symbols.meaning: The variable of the polynomial ring modulo z^r+1, which the source writes as y.
symbols.quote: Here $z$ is the polynomial variable, which the source writes as $y$.

symbols.name: coefficient count
symbols.meaning: The number of coefficients in a record, a power of two.
symbols.quote: One coordinate is stored as a polynomial in $z$ modulo $z^r+1$, where $r$, the number of coefficients, is a power of two.

relations.quote: The theorem refutes [The n log n optimality conjecture](n-log-n-conjecture.md) in this model.
The theorem is stated in the [Fixed-tape machine model](fixed-tape-model.md), so neither the alphabet nor the number of tapes depends on $n$.
Its time is measured by the [Running time cost](running-time-cost.md) of $A$, written $T_A(n)$, the largest number of steps $A$ takes on an input of length $n$.
The bound is stated with the [Logarithm](logarithm.md) to base two.
The theorem handles small inputs by [Schoolbook multiplication](schoolbook-multiplication.md), which is quadratic in the number of digits.

relations.predicate: gets its power saving from the
relations.quote: The theorem gets its power saving from the [Rank-saving recursion](rank-saving-recursion.md).
The theorem reduces exact multiplication to [Radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of short integer coefficients.
The theorem keeps its permutations inside a [Transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md).

relations.predicate: lays out its transforms by a
relations.quote: The theorem lays out its transforms by a [Transform layout](transform-layout.md), which places the selected bits of all transform axes at a common offset.
The theorem adds selected bits by [Packed selected-bit addition](packed-bit-addition.md).
The theorem places coefficients on axes by a [Chinese-remainder map](chinese-remainder-map.md) that preserves convolution.
The theorem chooses its axis lengths by [Prime source lengths](prime-source-lengths.md), which are distinct odd primes close to powers of two.
The theorem turns the last coordinate into a polynomial by a [Phase twist](phase-twist.md).
The theorem computes the remaining axes by [Convolution over the polynomial ring](polynomial-ring-convolution.md).

relations.predicate: recovers the coefficients by rounding through
relations.quote: The theorem recovers the coefficients by rounding through [Exact coefficient recovery](recovery-and-error.md).
The theorem ends with [Carry propagation](carry-propagation.md), which turns the recovered coefficients into the exact binary product.
